newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey imposes 10 pct witholding tax on govt.paper.
newsitem.headline: Turkey imposes 10 pct witholding tax on govt.paper.

text.p: Turkey imposed a 10 percent witholding tax on interest income from Treasury bills and bonds to be issued with 1997 maturity from November 1, the official gazette said late on Thursday.
The tax will not apply to outstanding t-bills and bonds having 1997 maturities, according to the cabinet decree published in gazette.
T-bill and bond yields dived by around three percentage points in the bond market as the decree buoyed market demand for outstanding papers.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan had announced government plans to charge witholding tax on interest income from state papers with 1997 maturities as part of the government's second revenue-raising package unveiled on September 19.

This caused banks to rush to buy t-bills and bonds from Treasury auctions because the government said the tax would not go into effect before a related government decree was pubished in the official gazzette and would not be retroactive.
The treasury has sold a total 907 trillion lira of paper with 1997 maturities in four auctions since September 19 in response to a record 1,900 trillion lira offer from the banks.
The treasury also managed to lower yields and gradually raise the maturity to 365-days from 196-days due to strong demand in the last four auctions.
According to the resource package, the government expects a 170 trillion lira income from the witholding tax in 1997.
